column1: # OWASP ZAP rule tuning for the API-Scan profile.
# Format, conventions, and WHO READS THIS FILE: see zap-rules.tsv. In short —
# `scripts/security/zap_gate.py` reads it, ZAP does not, only IGNORE is honoured,
# and every IGNORE needs an expiry with an approver plus an explicit
# This file is intentionally empty in Phase 1. Tuning entries are added

column4: # expires 2027-03-14 — approved by operator (2026-09-14). scope=/api/v1/privacy/email-change/confirm False positive, measured rather than judged: PrivacyService.confirm_email_change hashes `token` with sha256().hexdigest() BEFORE any lookup, so no attacker-controlled character reaches a query; the lookup is AQL with a bind parameter against ArangoDB; and the only SQL in the codebase (TimescaleDB) is static module constants executed with params. Reported by runs 34504023147 (#1376) and 34528880950 (#1389) — same endpoint, same parameter, same rule, twice. ZAP fires because every invalid token yields the identical error, so its boolean probe sees no difference between the true and false payloads; that uniformity is the endpoint's own no-oracle property (REQ-049 §2.4), not a symptom. The scope is this one path: rule 40018 keeps running everywhere else, and a finding at any other URL still blocks. If the nightly full-scan ever reports the same instance — it targets frontend:8080, whose nginx proxies /api/ to the backend — this row belongs in zap-rules.tsv as well; the scope is a path and matches either host. It is not pre-emptively added there, because a suppression is justified by a finding and the gate reports one that matches nothing.

# expires 2027-03-26 — approved by operator (2026-09-26). scope=/api/v1/auth/device-pairing/redeem False positive, measured rather than judged: AuthService.redeem_device_pairing's code store (IDevicePairingCodeStore) is Redis, not a database — there is no query for any attacker-controlled character to reach. `device_name` passes only `_validate_device_name` (a max-length check) and is then stored verbatim on the created session document, after the code has already been consumed and the account resolved via `record.user_key` (server-controlled, never from the request). The account lookup itself is `UserRepository.get_by_key`, a keyed ArangoDB read with no dynamic AQL construction. ZAP's boolean-pair evidence shows the triggering request answered 429 (Too Many Requests, per run 36235764467/#1908) — the route is rate-limited (`@limiter.limit(settings.rate_limit_device_pairing_redeem)`), and the differential response the rule read as "successfully restricting the data" is the rate limiter's own throttling between the two close-together probe requests, not a query outcome. The scope is this one path: rule 40018 keeps running everywhere else.
